text: You are Rahim, a hardworking rickshaw puller in Dhaka. Every day is a struggle to earn enough taka to feed your wife and three children. You usually try to stay out of politics, knowing that a single day without work means your family goes hungry. But as the streets you know so well transform into battlegrounds, avoiding the revolution becomes impossible.

text: You survived the turmoil, keeping your family safe and your rickshaw intact. Though you didn't participate in the uprising, you hope the new government will remember the poor.
Your small but brave actions—ferrying the injured and helping the youth—made you an unsung hero of the revolution. You proved that every citizen holds the power to change a nation.

Your bravery came at a high cost. Your rickshaw was heavily damaged in the clashes, plunging you into deep debt. Yet, as you watch the youth celebrate their freedom, you feel a tearful sense of pride.
